reminderStage6Title: Baby is 6 months old: daily protein portions
reminderStage6Body: Offer a total of 10 g of meat, fish or egg each day, and also vary with legumes. If not done yet, do not delay well-cooked egg, peanut and other allergens.
reminderStage9Title: Baby is 9 months old: progressing with pieces
reminderStage9Body: Depending on your baby’s abilities, offer very soft pieces: well-cooked vegetables, ripe avocado and well-cooked pasta. Always seated and supervised.
reminderStage12Title: Baby is 1 year old: adapted family meals
reminderStage12Body: Baby gradually shares adapted family meals: no added salt, limited sweet foods and safely cut pieces. Milk stays around 500 mL/day.
reminderStaleDiversityBody: Resume at your own pace: offer a food not yet tried to broaden flavours gradually.
reminderPendingAllergenBody: Once complementary feeding has started, this allergen should not be delayed. Offer it in an age-appropriate form.
reminderRepeatExposureBody: Taste acceptance is built through repetition: up to 10 times for some foods, always without pressure.

landingFaqQ1: When should I start weaning my baby?
landingFaqA1: French guidance (HCSP 2020 and Santé publique France) recommends starting between 4 completed months and 6 months, never before 4 months and without waiting beyond 6 months.
landingFaqQ2: Which allergens should be introduced early?
landingFaqA2: Once complementary feeding has started, allergens should not be delayed. Preventive evidence is strongest for well-cooked egg and peanut. The app tracks 12 allergens from the EU labelling list; crustaceans, molluscs, celery and mustard have no specific preventive timetable. Soy products are discouraged before age 3.
landingFaqQ3: Do I have to choose between purées and baby-led weaning?
landingFaqA3: No. The French Society of Paediatrics does not favour one method. For baby-led weaning, the child needs the required motor skills; pieces must be safe, intake sufficient and supervision constant.
landingFaqQ4: Which foods should be avoided at each age?
landingFaqA4: Before age 1: no honey and no cow’s milk as the main drink. Before age 3: no added salt or soy. Before age 5: no raw milk, raw or undercooked egg, meat, fish or shellfish, and no whole nuts. Round or hard foods must always be prepared and cut to reduce choking risk. Delay sweet products and prefer water.
landingFaqA5: Yes. Diversif is open source, self-hosted, free, and ad-free. Your data stays on your own server or host.

guideSeoTitle: Complementary feeding guide: babies from 4 months to 3 years · Diversif
guideSeoDescription: A sourced, comprehensive guide: 10 golden rules, 4 age-based stages, 12 tracked allergens, textures, foods to avoid, and what to do if a reaction occurs.
aideWhatBody: Diversif helps you through your baby’s food diversification: log every food you offer, track 12 allergens, vary tastes and textures, and keep a record of reactions. The app is self-hosted and ad-free — your data stays with you.
aideSharingBody: Tracking is meant to be shared. From your Profile, open the child’s settings and generate an invite code, then send the link to the other parent. Once they’ve created an account and accepted the invitation, you both see the same log and can each record meals and reactions. The code expires after 7 days and can be used only once.
aideTrustBody: The guidance draws on authoritative sources: HCSP, Santé publique France, ANSES, ESPGHAN, WHO, the French Paediatric Society, and the LEAP and EAT studies.
